##  Update July 17

With hotfixes that are now live, the following have been added to Burning Crusade Classic:

##  User Interface

* **Raid Frames**
  
    + Added interface options for Raid Frames to select health bar color and background color.
    + Added interface options for Raid Frames to show or hide dispellable debuff indicators (default: off).
    + Edit Mode: Added Layout Template, Opacity, and Aura Icon Size options to Raid Frames
+ Edit Mode: Fixed a bug where some aura icons would appear larger in the Edit Mode Raid Frame preview.
* **Nameplates**
  
    + Added interface option to color friendly or enemy nameplates based on player class color.
* Fixed a bug where the item comparison tooltip was always showing, instead of only showing when you held down Shift.

Hello,

This week, we updated Burning Crusade Classic Anniversary from patch 2.5.5 to patch 2.5.6. Although this patch was almost entirely to support critical service systems, it also included changes to nameplates and raid frames. We’d like to tell you about these changes, highlight options you have to edit some of the user interface (UI), and look forward to patch 1.15.9 coming to WoW Classic soon.

**UI Using Shared Code**

All versions of WoW Classic share code with modern World of Warcraft.

...

Similar to this week’s Burning Crusade Classic Anniversary patch, the WoW Classic games (Classic Era, Season of Discovery, Hardcore) will receive a similar patch with the start of weekly regional maintenance the week of July 19. As with the Burning Crusade Classic Anniversary patch, this patch will bring in Edit Mode and changes to players’ nameplates and raid frames to the WoW Classic games.

Some third-party addons may experience errors until they are updated by their authors. As all versions of World of Warcraft share most of their UI code, the addon API in 1.15.9 very closely matches the addon API from 2.5.6. For addon authors, we encourage you to use 2.5.6 as an environment for updating addons to be compatible with 1.15.9.

We will continue to refine our updates in the future, so that we’re providing additional options for players to modify settings wherever possible.

Thank you, as always, for your passion and feedback.

# User Interface Update Coming to WoW Classic Era, SoD & Hardcore

Luxrah [Luxrah](https://www.warcrafttavern.com/participant/luxrah/) • Published July 10, 2026

TBC Anniversary Edition recieved an update to its UI this week, bringing Nameplate and Raid Frame options from WoW: Midnight into the Classic game mode. Blizzard has announced their plans to add these features to Classic WoW within the next couple of weeks. They’ll also be implementing Edit Mode, which has already made its way into other versions of Classic.

The update will bring all Classic Era, Season of Discovery, and Hardcore modes into Patch 1.15.9. Many addons will need to be updated to accomodate the new features.

* Top community UI profiles you can import today
* Blizzard’s new Edit Mode features and how to maximize them
* Essential addons that complement any UI setup
* My personal recommendations based on hundreds of hours of testing
* Step-by-step setup tips for each major framework

## Understanding What Makes a “Good” WoW UI

Before I throw addon names at you, let’s talk philosophy. The best UI isn’t the prettiest one or the one your favorite streamer uses — it’s the one that puts critical information where your eyes naturally go while hiding everything else.

The golden rule: Your character should be surrounded by the information you need most. Health, resources, important cooldowns, and boss mechanics should live in your screen’s center-lower area. Everything else — chat, damage meters, minimap — gets pushed to the edges.

...

Why It Stands Out: If you’ve ever looked at WoW’s default UI and thought “this looks like it was designed in 2004” (because it was), GW2 UI is the answer. It’s genuinely beautiful while remaining functional.

My Testing Experience: I ran GW2 UI for about three months. The aesthetic grew on me immediately, but I eventually switched back to ElvUI because I needed more granular control over my raid frames. That said, for casual content and open-world gameplay, nothing looks better.

Pros:

* Stunning visual design
* Feels like a modern MMO interface
* Good performance optimization
* Unique look that stands out

Cons:

* Less customization than ElvUI-based options
* Some features feel less polished for high-end content
* Smaller community means fewer resources

Best For: Casual players, collectors, and anyone prioritizing aesthetics.

## Blizzard Edit Mode — The Underrated Option

Press enter or click to view image in full size
What It Is: WoW’s built-in UI customization system, dramatically expanded in recent patches.

Why It Stands Out: With the updates through The War Within and into 2026, Blizzard’s Edit Mode has become legitimately good. You can now reposition almost everything, resize frames, and even import/export layouts — no addons required.

My Testing Experience: I was skeptical until I actually spent time with it. For players who don’t want addon dependencies or who play on multiple computers, Edit Mode is now a viable primary option. I tested Dwalland’s UI 2.0 profile recently, and it’s impressive what you can achieve with zero addons.

Pros:

* No addon maintenance or updates needed
* Officially supported (won’t break with patches)
* Surprisingly deep customization now
* Includes new features like boss timeline and damage meter
* Perfect for minimalists

Cons:

* Still less powerful than dedicated addons
* Some elements can’t be modified
* Community profiles are harder to find

...

After testing dozens of configurations, here’s what I’ve settled on:

Base: ElvUI with heavy customization Nameplates: Plater with custom scripts Raid Frames: ElvUI’s built-in frames (surprisingly good once configured) WeakAuras: Class-specific rotation helper plus boss mechanics Damage Meter: Details, minimized until I need it

The key insight that changed everything: I stopped trying to see all information all the time. Now my UI shows different things based on context. In combat, I see what I need to fight. Out of combat, I see chat and social stuff. This “contextual UI” approach — hiding elements until they’re relevant — reduced my screen clutter by probably 60%.

## Quick Setup Guide

1. Choose your framework (ElvUI for control, ToxiUI for convenience, Edit Mode for simplicity)
2. Import a community profile as your starting point
3. Play for a week before making changes — you need to see what’s actually missing
4.
Adjust one thing at a time — resist the urge to overhaul everything at once
5. Export your profile once you’re happy (seriously, do this)

## Frequently Asked Questions

What’s the best UI for beginners ? ToxiUI or Blizzard’s Edit Mode. Both work well out of the box without requiring extensive configuration knowledge.

Does UI choice affect performance? Minimally with modern hardware. ElvUI is well-optimized. The bigger FPS killers are usually WeakAuras with poor scripting or nameplates showing too much information.

How do I import someone else’s UI? For ElvUI: /elvui → Profiles → Import. For Edit Mode: Escape → Edit Mode → Import from the dropdown menu.

Should I use ElvUI or stick with default? Depends on your goals. Default (with Edit Mode) is now viable for casual play. ElvUI remains superior for serious raiding or M+.

What about UI for PvP? PvP benefits from minimal, centered information. GladiusEx for arena frames plus a clean ElvUI setup works well.
Keep your screen as clear as possible.

How often should I update my UI? Check for addon updates weekly. Major overhauls should wait until you identify actual problems — don’t change things just because you’re bored.

Can I use multiple UI profiles for different characters? Yes! ElvUI supports per-character profiles. I run different setups for my healer versus my DPS characters.

What’s the deal with Dwalland UI 2.0? It’s a solid Edit Mode profile that leverages Blizzard’s new features like the boss timeline and built-in damage meter. Great option if you want to go addon-free.

## Final Thoughts

The “best” UI for WoW is the one you stop noticing because it just works. You shouldn’t be fighting your interface — you should be fighting bosses. Start with a proven community profile, play with it for a while, then make incremental adjustments based on what you actually need.

And honestly? The time you save with a proper UI setup compounds.
Every pull where you don’t die to avoidable damage, every dungeon where you notice the interrupt in time, every raid where you see the mechanic coming — that’s your UI doing its job.

# Blizzard has modernized some parts of the WoW Classic Era and TBC Classic anniversary realms user interface

By [Nick Marino](https://blizzardwatch.com/author/nmarino/)

Over the last week, Blizzard [implemented user interface changes](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/t/user-interface-updates-in-classic/2325408) to [_World of Warcraft Classic_](https://blizzardwatch.com/category/warcraft/wow-classic/) realms and [_The Burning Crusade Classic_ anniversary](https://blizzardwatch.com/tag/tbc-classic-anniversary-realms/) realms that specifically affect the look of character name plates and raid frames, and also affect all _Classic_ realms including [Era](https://blizzardwatch.com/tag/classic-era/) , [Season of Discovery](https://blizzardwatch.com/tag/season-of-discovery/) , and [Hardcore](https://blizzardwatch.com/tag/wow-classic-hardcore/) .
Blizzard has communicated these user interface changes, it feels more like a modernized update to the _Classic_ world and we’ve broken down what they are, how they affect the game now, and what changes could be in store for the future.

## What are the changes and why were they made?

* Raid Frames
  
    + Added options to select health bar color and background color
    + Added options to show or hide dispellable debuff indicators
* Edit Mode
  
    + Added Layout Template, Opacity, and Aura Icon Size Options
* Nameplates
  
    + Added option to color friendly or enemy nameplates based on player class color

There were also bugs affecting the size of the aura icons in the edit mode preview and the item comparison tooltip always showing that were fixed but the main thing really stands out is that the appearance of nameplate and raid frame are more in line with the styles used in _World of Warcraft Midnight.

...

* Disabling Raid Frame Dispel Highlights:
  
    + /script C\_CVar.SetCVar(“raidFramesDispelIndicatorOverlay”, 0);

So, what’s the overall goal here? From a development standpoint, this shared code provides the easiest route for Blizzard to support and maintain each game in the long run despite the differing aspects of their time-locked state. The downside here is the permanence of the UI changes integrated that have no real visual rollback option. Sure, Edit Mode exists and has a _Classic_ pre-set, but even that itself is a tool from the retail version and its existence in _Classic_ is still a shift to the modern day.

Could Blizzard be moving to fully integrate retail _WoW_ UI into _Classic_ ? Maybe, but since the appeal of _Classic_ is the nostalgic, old-school look and feel, it’d be a bad overall move to do that and it makes more sense to preserve that aesthetic where possible.
